claim: Overproduction of proteins triggers cellular defects.
source: Overproduction (op) of proteins triggers cellular defects.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general principle.

claim: One consequence of protein overproduction is the protein burden/cost, which is produced by overloading the protein synthesis process.
source: One of the consequences of overproduction is the protein burden/cost, which is produced by an overloading of the protein synthesis process.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background knowledge.

claim: Extreme overproduction of a gratuitous protein causes growth defects.
source: Extreme overproduction of a gratuitous protein that has no cellular function causes growth defects, which, at least in part, appears to be caused by overloading the cellular resources for protein synthesis (Dong et al., 1995; Snoep et al., 1995; Stoebel et al., 2008; Makanae et al., 2013; Shah et al., 2013; Kafri et al., 2016; Moriya, 2015; Eguchi et al., 2018; Scott et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Limiting functions defining the protein burden are thought to be the translational process upon nitrogen limitation and the transcriptional process upon phosphate limitation.
source: Limiting functions defining the protein burden are thought to be the translational process upon nitrogen limitation, and the transcriptional process upon phosphate limitation (Kafri et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kafri et al., 2016.

claim: Fluorescent proteins such as EGFP, Venus, and mCherry do not have any physiological activity in yeast cells and are considered gratuitous proteins.
source: Fluorescent proteins, such as EGFP, Venus, and mCherry, do not have any physiological activity in yeast cells and thus are considered gratuitous proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Overproduction of fluorescent proteins triggers a protein burden.
source: Therefore, these fluorescent proteins are believed to be produced at the highest possible levels in yeast cells, and their overproduction triggers a protein burden (Makanae et al., 2013; Kafri et al., 2016; Eguchi et al., 2018; Farkas et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Modifications to EGFP such as adding a degradation signal, misfolding mutations, or adding localization signals reduces its expression limit.
source: Modifications to EGFP, such as adding a degradation signal, misfolding mutations, or adding localization signals, reduces its expression limit, probably because these modifications overload limited resources for the degradation, folding, and localization processes, respectively (Geiler-Samerotte et al., 2011; Makanae et al., 2013; Kintaka et al., 2016; Eguchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Hsp70-associated chaperones contribute to the protein burden by minimizing the damaging impact of the overproduction of a gratuitous protein.
source: Through the analysis of these strains, and conditions exacerbating the protein burden, the authors concluded that Hsp70-associated chaperones contribute to the protein burden by minimizing the damaging impact of the overproduction of a gratuitous protein.
evidence: This claim is based on conclusions from a previous study by Farkas et al., 2018.

claim: A strain harboring the pTOW40836-TDH3pro-GFP plasmid shows growth defects under –Ura conditions.
source: While a strain harboring this plasmid shows growth defects even under –Ura conditions (Figure 1C), the strain shows more growth defects under –Leu/Ura conditions (Figure 1D), presumably because the copy number increase leads to an increase in GFP production, and probably causes a stronger protein burden-associated growth defect (Eguchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C and cited literature.

claim: The strain harboring pTOW40836-TDH3pro-GFP shows more growth defects under –Leu/Ura conditions than under –Ura conditions.
source: While a strain harboring this plasmid shows growth defects even under –Ura conditions (Figure 1C), the strain shows more growth defects under –Leu/Ura conditions (Figure 1D), presumably because the copy number increase leads to an increase in GFP production, and probably causes a stronger protein burden-associated growth defect (Eguchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: The copy numbers of pTOW40836 under –Ura and –Leu/Ura conditions are around 10 and 30 copies per cell, respectively.
source: The copy numbers of this plasmid under –Ura and –Leu/Ura conditions are around 10 and 30 copies per cell, respectively (Eguchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Eguchi et al., 2018.

claim: The reproducibility of the DMA experiments was lower in –Ura conditions (r = 0.17) than in –Leu/Ura conditions (r = 0.36).
source: The reproducibility of the DMA experiments was lower in –Ura conditions (r = 0.17), whereas it was higher in –Leu/Ura conditions (r = 0.36).
evidence: This claim is based on correlation analysis of experimental replicates.

claim: The reproducibility of the TSA experiments was higher in both –Ura and –Leu/Ura conditions (r = 0.42 and 0.53).
source: The reproducibility of the TSA experiments was higher in both –Ura and –Leu/Ura conditions (r = 0.42 and 0.53).
evidence: This claim is based on correlation analysis of experimental replicates.

claim: Conditions which cause severe growth defects produce the most reproducible GI scores.
source: Thus, the conditions which cause severe growth defects produce the most reproducible GI scores.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the reproducibility data.

claim: The GI scores obtained by this study did not show correlation with those from the Farkas study (r = –0.01 and –0.07).
source: The GI scores obtained by our analysis did not show correlation with those from the Farkas study (r = –0.01 and –0.07, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is based on correlation analysis comparing two studies.

claim: A group of temperature-sensitive mutants showed greater growth defects under –Leu/Ura conditions than under –Ura conditions in the vector control experiments.
source: During the screening, we noticed that a group of temperature-sensitive mutants showed greater growth defects under –Leu/Ura conditions than under –Ura conditions in the vector control experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the screening data.

claim: The gene ontology term 'DNA replication preinitiation complex [GO:0031261]' was significantly over-represented in the mutated genes showing growth defects under high-copy conditions.
source: The gene ontology (GO) term 'DNA replication preinitiation complex [GO:0031261]' was significantly over-represented in the mutated genes (seven genes, p=1.47E–05).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis with a significant p-value.

claim: The GFP-op_negative 71 genes (79 mutants) were significantly enriched in GO categories related to cytoskeletal organization and polarization.
source: The GFP-op_negaitive 71 genes (79 mutants) were significantly enriched in GO categories related to cytoskeletal organization and polarization (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: One hundred GFP-op_positive genes (100 mutants) were enriched in genes involved in RNA 3′-end processing and the transcription factor complex.
source: One hundred GFP-op_positive genes (100 mutants) were enriched in genes involved in RNA 3′-end processing and the transcription factor complex (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Of 13 mutants of the TRAMP complex and nuclear exosome subunits, seven showed positive GIs with average scores greater than 0.2.
source: Of 13 mutants, seven showed positive GIs with average scores greater than 0.2.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of GI scores for specific mutants.

claim: In total, 20 out of 38 mutants of the mediator-RNA polymerase II preinitiation complex subunits showed positive GIs with average scores greater than 0.2.
source: In total, 20 out of 38 mutants showed positive GIs with average scores greater than 0.2.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of GI scores for specific mutants.

claim: Mutants with enhanced growth defects upon GFP overproduction (GFP-op_negative mutants) were more likely to produce less GFP (GFP_L).
source: Mutants with enhanced growth defects upon GFP overproduction (GFP-op_negative mutants) were more likely to produce less GFP (GFP_L) (Figure 4C, p=4.7E-11, Student's t-test), indicating that the limit of GFP overproduction in these cells was lower than in other cells.
evidence: This claim is based on statistical analysis (Student's t-test) of GFP expression levels.

claim: Eleven out of 13 GFP-op_negative mutants categorized as 'cellular bud [GO:0005933]' were also GFP_L.
source: Eleven out of 13 GFP-op_negative mutants categorized as 'cellular bud [GO:0005933]' were also GFP_L (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 2A) (the GFP levels for each strain in this category are shown in Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of GFP expression levels in specific mutants.

claim: GFP-op_positive and GFP_L mutants were significantly enriched in 'RNA polymerase II transcriptional factor complex [GO:0090575]'.
source: However, GFP-op_positive and GFP_L mutants were significantly enriched in 'RNA polymerase II transcriptional factor complex [GO:0090575]', suggesting that these mutants may simply cause the reduction of GFP production, but not decrease the sensitivity to the protein burden.
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis.

claim: The 14 mutants showing growth advantage enhanced by GFP overproduction were significantly enriched in genes of the DASH complex [GO:0042729].
source: The 14 mutants were significantly enriched in genes of the DASH complex [GO:0042729] (Supplementary file 3), including ask1-2, dad2-9, and spc34-5 out of the seven DASH complex mutants analyzed (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Only 12% (81/688) of mutants showed shared GIs between GFP and tGFP.
source: To our surprise, only 12% (81/688) of mutants showed shared GIs between GFP and tGFP.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of genetic interaction profiles.

claim: Mutants negatively interacting with tGFP-op and NES-tGFP-op but not GFP-op (Cluster 4) were strongly enriched in annotations of 'cytosolic proteasome complex [GO:0031597]'.
source: Mutants negatively interacting with tGFP-op and NES-tGFP-op but not GFP-op (Cluster 4) were strongly enriched in annotations of 'cytosolic proteasome complex [GO:0031597]' (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis of clustered mutants.

claim: GI scores of mutants in 'proteasome complex [GO:0000502]' were significantly lower in the tGFP-op and NES-tGFP-op experiments than in the GFP-op experiment.
source: GI scores of mutants in 'proteasome complex [GO:0000502]' were significantly lower in the tGFP-op and NES-tGFP-op experiments than in the GFP-op experiment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is based on statistical comparison of GI scores across experiments.

claim: Overproduction of NES-tGFP had strong negative GIs with mutants in the major nuclear export factors (Crm1, Gsp1, Rna1, and Yrb1).
source: Overproduction of NES-tGFP had strong negative GIs with mutants in the major nuclear export factors (Crm1, Gsp1, Rna1, and Yrb1; Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is based on genetic interaction data shown in figures.

claim: tGFP-op (and NES-tGFP-op) had negative GIs with mutants in proteasome components but GFP-op did not.
source: tGFP-op (and NES-tGFP-op) had negative GIs with mutants in proteasome components but GFP-op did not (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is based on genetic interaction data shown in figures.

claim: tGFP and NES-tGFP form aggregates, but not GFP.
source: tGFP and NES-tGFP form aggregates, but not GFP (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is based on microscopy observations shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The amount of tGFP (and NES-tGFP) was about 4% of GFP.
source: Indeed, when we investigated the abundance of GFP and tGFP by Western blotting, the amount of tGFP (and NES-tGFP) was about 4% of GFP (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is based on Western blot quantification shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Giant condensates were present only in the cells overproducing tGFP and NES-tGFP.
source: We found that giant condensate were present only in the cells overproducing tGFP and NES-tGFP (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is based on microscopy observations shown in Figure 6C.

claim: About 1% of GFP was found in the precipitation fraction, whereas 14% of tGFP was found in the precipitation fraction.
source: About 1% of GFP was found in the precipitation fraction, whereas 14% of tGFP was found in the precipitation fraction.
evidence: This claim is based on cell fractionation and Western blot analysis.

claim: Western blotting with anti-ubiquitin antibodies detected ubiquitinated high-molecular-weight proteins in the precipitates of tGFP-op.
source: Western blotting with anti-ubiquitin antibodies detected ubiquitinated high-molecular-weight proteins in the precipitates of tGFP-op (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is based on Western blot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Hsp70 (Ssa1/Ssa2) and the glycolytic enzymes Fba1 and Eno2 were particularly abundant in the precipitates of tGFP-op.
source: Among them, Hsp70 (Ssa1/Ssa2) and the glycolytic enzymes Fba1 and Eno2 were particularly abundant in the precipitates of tGFP-op.
evidence: This claim is based on LC-MS/MS proteome analysis.

claim: Components of the proteasome were identified in the precipitation, albeit in trace amounts, and tended to be more abundant in the precipitation of tGFP-op than in the vector control.
source: Components of the proteasome were also identified, albeit in trace amounts, and tended to be more abundant in the precipitation of tGFP-op than in the vector control.
evidence: This claim is based on LC-MS/MS proteome analysis.

claim: Among obtained 501 morphological parameters, only four parameters showed significant differences over the vector control, and three of them (A120_A1B, ACV7-1_A, and A122_A1B) were actin-related parameters.
source: Among obtained 501 morphological parameters, only four parameters showed significant differences over the vector control, and three of them (A120_A1B, ACV7-1_A, and A122_A1B) were actin-related parameters (Figure 7A–D).
evidence: This claim is based on morphological analysis using CalMorph.

claim: The cells overexpressing GFP contained increased actin patch regions.
source: The cells contained increased actin patch regions, supporting the idea that the protein burden interacts with actin function.
evidence: This claim is based on interpretation of morphological data.

claim: Only harmless proteins like GFP can be produced up to the ultimate expression levels that cause the protein burden.
source: Only harmless proteins like GFP can be produced up to the ultimate expression levels that cause the protein burden, which seems to be related to actin functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Other proteins, localized or aggregative, can be produced at far lower levels than the level which causes the protein burden because their overproduction overloads localization or protein degradation resources which are more limited than the protein synthesis resource.
source: Other proteins, localized or aggregative, can be produced at far lower levels than the level which causes the protein burden because their overproduction overloads localization or protein degradation resources which are more limited than the protein synthesis resource.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The protein burden is caused by perturbations to protein synthesis.
source: Protein burden is therefore thought to be caused by perturbations to protein synthesis.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion.

claim: The analysis of genetic interactions did not provide a clear link to perturbations to the synthetic process.
source: Our analysis of genetic interactions, however, did not provide a clear link to perturbations to the synthetic process; our results suggest that protein burden causes an unexpected perturbation of actin function.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the Discussion.

claim: The expression limits of tGFP and NES-tGFP were much lower than those of GFP.
source: In fact, the expression limits of tGFP, which undergoes degradation by aggregation and ubiquitination (probably by misfolding), and NES-tGFP, which is transported outside the nucleus, were much lower than those of GFP.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the Discussion.

claim: The expression limits of tGFP and NES-tGFP were about 0.6% of the total proteins.
source: Since their expression limits were about 4% of GFP (Figure 6B), it can be estimated that their expression limits are about 0.6% of the total proteins.
evidence: This is calculated from the Western blot data in Figure 6B.

claim: NES-tGFP triggers growth defects at a lower expression level than unmodified tGFP.
source: NES-tGFP triggers growth defects at a lower expression level than unmodified tGFP (Kintaka et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kintaka et al., 2016.

claim: Mutants harboring genetic interactions with tGFP-op should be different from those with NES-tGFP-op if the protein burden can only be triggered by a harmless protein like GFP.
source: If the protein burden can only be triggered by a harmless protein like GFP, mutants harboring genetic interactions with tGFP-op should be different from those with NES-tGFP-op, and the comparison of those mutants will identify consequences specific to the protein burden.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: Mutants harboring negative genetic interactions with NES-tGFP should contain limiting factors of the nuclear export and essential factors affected by the overloading of nuclear export.
source: Moreover, mutants harboring negative genetic interactions should contain limiting factors of the nuclear export and essential factors affected by the overloading of nuclear export.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction.

claim: The DASH complex binds to microtubules and is involved in the distribution of chromosomes.
source: The DASH complex binds to microtubules and is involved in the distribution of chromosomes (Jenni and Harrison, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jenni and Harrison, 2018.

claim: The protein burden may impact numerous processes beyond chaperone-related processes.
source: Chaperone genes, however, constitute only a relatively small fraction of the deletion strains isolated in the study, and thus the protein burden may impact numerous other processes.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that chaperone genes are a small fraction of isolated strains.

claim: The relationship between actin and translational machinery might explain the connection between protein burden and actin cytoskeleton perturbation.
source: This relationship might be a result of the long-known connection between actin and translational machinery Kim and Coulombe, 2010; the protein burden-triggered growth defects might involve the perturbation of the actin cytoskeleton via translational factors like eEF1A, which can bundle actin fibers (Munshi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation based on known connections and cited literature.

claim: tGFP has a high probability of misfolding during translation.
source: A larger molecule may increase the likelihood of misfolding during translation, or the presence of a repeating structure may increase intermolecular interactions and trigger the creation of large aggregates.
evidence: This is speculated based on the properties of tGFP.

claim: Ssa1/Ssa2 is required for proteasome assembly.
source: In addition, since Ssa1/Ssa2 is required for proteasome assembly (Hammack et al., 2017), a depletion of these proteins would lower the amount of proteasomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hammack et al., 2017.

claim: Large amounts of Ssa1/Ssa2 were detected in the tGFP-op precipitates.
source: Based on the results of the proteome analysis, we believe that 4 is particularly likely, given that large amounts of Ssa1/Ssa2 were detected in the tGFP-op precipitates.
evidence: This claim is based on proteome analysis results.

claim: The high copy number of the vector (more than 100 copies per cell under –Leu/Ura conditions) probably produces limitations of the replication initiation complex by sequestering the complex to the replication origins of the plasmids.
source: The vector copy number is more than 100 copies per cell under –Leu/Ura conditions (Makanae et al., 2013; Eguchi et al., 2018). This high copy number probably produces limitations of the replication initiation complex by sequestering the complex to the replication origins of the plasmids (the explanation of the fitness reduction is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is an inference based on known plasmid copy numbers and the properties of replication initiation complexes.

claim: Negative GIs of 6 out of 7 deletion mutants from this screening were confirmed by independent growth measurements in liquid medium.
source: Indeed, our conditions produced more variance in the GI scores and thus identified more mutants showing stronger GIs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B), and we found that negative GIs of 6 out of 7 deletion mutants from our screening were confirmed by independent growth measurements in the liquid medium, while all six mutants isolated by the previous study (Farkas et al., 2018) were not (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is based on independent validation experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: All six mutants isolated by the Farkas et al. study were not confirmed by independent growth measurements in liquid medium.
source: Indeed, our conditions produced more variance in the GI scores and thus identified more mutants showing stronger GIs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B), and we found that negative GIs of 6 out of 7 deletion mutants from our screening were confirmed by independent growth measurements in the liquid medium, while all six mutants isolated by the previous study (Farkas et al., 2018) were not (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is based on independent validation experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Overproduction of yEGFP resulted in increased growth inhibition (cost) due to amino acid dilution.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3G, overproduction of yEGFP also resulted in increased growth inhibition (cost) due to amino acid dilution, although the degree of cost differed between the two fluorescent proteins.
evidence: This claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3G.

claim: The difference between the analysis of Farkas et al. and this study may be due to the difference in properties between yEGFP and yEVenus.
source: We cannot dismiss the possibility that the difference between the analysis of Farkas et al. and ours is due to the difference in properties between our GFP (yEGFP) and yEVenus.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility to explain differences between studies.

claim: GFP is about 15% of the total protein in the cell under –Leu/Ura conditions with pTOW40836-TDH3pro-GFP.
source: In –Leu/Ura conditions, pTOW40836-TDH3pro-GFP has a copy number of about 30, at which time GFP is about 15% of the total protein in the cell (C, in GFP-op/WT) (Eguchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Eguchi et al., 2018.

claim: Among the mutants that had a negative genetic interaction with NES-tGFP-op, the mutants with lower GFP expression (NES-tGFP_L) were enriched for genes involved in nuclear protein transport.
source: Among the mutants that had a negative genetic interaction with NES-tGFP-op, the mutants with lower GFP expression (NES-tGFP_L) were enriched for genes involved in nuclear protein transport (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: All mutants in Cluster 3 (crm1-1, gsp1-162, rna1-1, rna1-s116f, and yrb1-52) were included in the NES-tGFP_L group.
source: Furthermore, all mutants in Cluster 3 in Figure 5D (crm1-1, gsp1-162, rna1-1, rna1-s116f, and yrb1-52) were included in this group (Figure 5E, Supplementary file 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of GFP expression levels in specific mutants.

claim: The identification of nuclear protein transport mutants as specifically sensitive to overproduction of NES-tGFP can be considered as a proof of concept for this study.
source: The identification of nuclear protein transport mutants as specifically sensitive to overproduction of NES-tGFP can be considered as a proof of concept for this study, and the results strongly support that the analysis of GFP-op and tGFP-op also allowed us to obtain mutants specifically associated with the physiological state of the cells triggered by the overproduction of them.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Overproduced tGFP is actively degraded by the proteasome in wild-type strains.
source: This suggests that overexpressed tGFP is actively degraded by the proteasome in the wild-type strains, whereas overaccumulation of undegraded tGFP occurs in proteasome mutations or that undegraded tGFP is cytotoxic in mutations of the proteasome.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that proteasome mutants show negative GIs with tGFP-op.

claim: Overaccumulation of undegraded tGFP occurs in proteasome mutations.
source: This suggests that overexpressed tGFP is actively degraded by the proteasome in the wild-type strains, whereas overaccumulation of undegraded tGFP occurs in proteasome mutations or that undegraded tGFP is cytotoxic in mutations of the proteasome.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that proteasome mutants show negative GIs with tGFP-op.

claim: Undegraded tGFP is cytotoxic in mutations of the proteasome.
source: This suggests that overexpressed tGFP is actively degraded by the proteasome in the wild-type strains, whereas overaccumulation of undegraded tGFP occurs in proteasome mutations or that undegraded tGFP is cytotoxic in mutations of the proteasome.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that proteasome mutants show negative GIs with tGFP-op.
